text: Python lets a class inherit from more than one parent at once — that's multiple inheritance.
Swimmer knows how to move, and Flyer knows how to fly, each a separate ability.
Duck inherits from both, mixing their abilities together and adding its own sound.
[chuckle] So a single duck can swim, fly, and quack, drawing methods from both parents at once.
[sniff] But what if two parents define the same method? Python needs a rule to decide which wins.
That rule is the Method Resolution Order, or MRO — the exact sequence Python searches for a method.
Duck's MRO lists itself first, then its parents left to right, then object at the very end.
[sigh] Python follows that order and stops at the first match, giving predictable, consistent behavior.
[groan] Multiple inheritance is powerful but can get tangled — many people prefer small, focused mixins to keep it clean.
